title: Cell structure of the walking coherent module weight
statement:
Use simplicial sets and nerves of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the ordinal-sum conventions of [def-coef-coherent-monad-modules]. Let $\Delta_+$ be the category of finite ordered sets, including the empty set, and monotone maps. Let $\Delta_\infty$ be the category of nonempty finite ordered sets and monotone maps preserving the last element. Put $D=N(\Delta_+)$ and $W=N(\Delta_\infty)$. Ordinal sum gives $D$ a simplicial monoid structure with empty unit and $W$ a left simplicial $D$-action. Regard $D$ itself as its regular left module. The map $j:D\to W$, given by adjoining a last singleton and extending each ordinal map by the identity on that singleton, is $D$-equivariant and bijective on vertices.

In the category of left simplicial $D$-modules, both $\varnothing\to W$ and $j:D\to W$ are small relative projective cell complexes. This means small transfinite composites, continuous at limit ordinals, of pushouts of coproducts of free-module maps
$$D\times\partial\Delta^n\longrightarrow D\times\Delta^n.$$
Both cell complexes permit $n\geq0$. In particular $W$ is a cellular weight for the one-object simplicial category with endomorphism simplicial monoid $D$.

source.place: Definition 6.1.6, Lemma 6.1.8, proof of Corollary 6.2.3, Observation 6.2.4, and Proposition 5.3.3 (collages and relative projective cells). Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this combinatorial weight lemma.

proof.text: Use the two displayed categories and their nerves from [def-coef-coherent-monad-modules]. Ordinal sum is strictly associative and has the empty ordinal as unit, so it induces a simplicial monoid D and a left D-action on W. Extending a monotone map by the identity at a newly adjoined terminal point commutes with ordinal sum; hence j is D-equivariant. Every nonempty finite ordinal is uniquely an augmented ordinal with one terminal point adjoined, so j is bijective on vertices. These are direct checks on maps of finite ordered sets.

Apply the free-orbit criterion [lem-coef-free-module-orbit-cell-filtration] with $M=D$. Its hypotheses at a successor stage are: a set of simplices $\sigma$ whose proper faces lie in the previous stage, such that $(m,\theta)\mapsto m\cdot\theta^*\sigma$, with $m$ a $D$-simplex and $\theta$ a surjection in the simplex category, is a bijection from the disjoint union over $\sigma$ onto the simplices (degenerate or not) of the new stage outside the old one. These are exactly the conditions that make the attaching square a pushout of a coproduct of free cells $D\times\partial\Delta^n\to D\times\Delta^n$. The criterion allows a set of cells at one stage, includes $n=0$ (whose boundary is empty), and requires unions at limit ordinals.

An $r$-simplex $x$ of $W$ is a string $x_0\to\cdots\to x_r$ of last-preserving maps $f_i$ of nonempty finite ordinals. A cut is a tuple $c=(c_0,\ldots,c_r)$ with $0\leq c_i<|x_i|$ such that each $f_i$ sends the first $c_i$ points into the first $c_{i+1}$ points and the remaining points into the remaining points; equivalently $x=d\cdot y$ with $d$ the $D$-string on the initial segments and $y$ the $W$-string on the complements (the complements are nonempty and $y$ still preserves last elements). The cuts are closed under componentwise maximum: if $c,c'$ are cuts and $c''=\max(c,c')$, monotonicity of $f_i$ gives both conditions for $c''$. A cut $c''\geq c$ of $x=d\cdot y$ restricts to the cut $c''-c$ of $y$, and conversely. Hence $y$ is left-reduced (its only cut is $0$) exactly when $c$ is the maximal cut of $x$, so $x=d\cdot y$ with $y$ left-reduced in exactly one way, and $d$ is determined as the restriction of $x$ to the cut. If $y=\theta^*\bar y$ is its Eilenberg--Zilber factorization ($\theta$ surjective, $\bar y$ nondegenerate, both unique), then $\bar y$ is left-reduced: a cut of $\bar y$ pulls back along $\theta$ to a cut of $y$, nonzero if it was; conversely a cut of $\theta^*\bar y$ is constant along the identity maps of a degeneracy, so reducedness is stable under degeneracies. Let $R$ be the set of nondegenerate left-reduced simplices of $W$. Then every simplex of $W$, degenerate or not, is $d\cdot\theta^*\sigma$ for exactly one triple ($d$ a $D$-simplex, $\theta$ surjective, $\sigma\in R$). The only reduced vertex is the singleton $[0]$, since every vertex $[k]$ has the maximal cut $k$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.8 and proof of Corollary 6.2.3; normal-form filtration of the walking module

proof.text: Let $X_n$ be the $D$-submodule of simplices whose triple has $\dim\sigma\leq n$, i.e. the submodule generated by the elements of $R$ of dimension at most $n$, and $X_{-1}=\varnothing$; this is a simplicial submodule because a face or degeneracy of $d\cdot\theta^*\sigma$ is $(\alpha^*d)\cdot\rho^*(\mu^*\sigma)$ for the factorization $\theta\alpha=\mu\rho$ ($\rho$ surjective, $\mu$ injective), and writing the face $\mu^*\sigma=d''\cdot\theta''^*\sigma''$ by step 3 gives the triple $(\alpha^*d\oplus\rho^*d'',\theta''\rho,\sigma'')$ with $\dim\sigma''\leq\dim\mu^*\sigma\leq\dim\sigma$ (it is the triple of step 3 because $\rho^*\theta''^*\sigma''$ is left-reduced). Take $R_n=\{\sigma\in R:\dim\sigma=n\}$. By step 3, $(d,\theta)\mapsto d\cdot\theta^*\sigma$ is a bijection onto $X_n\setminus X_{n-1}$; a proper face of $\sigma\in R_n$ is an $(n-1)$-simplex, whose own $\sigma'$ has dimension at most $n-1$, so it lies in $X_{n-1}$. The criterion gives a cell filtration of $\varnothing\to W$ of length $\omega$, with $\bigcup_nX_n=W$. For the relative map: $X_0$ consists of the simplices $d\cdot s^*[0]$, the strings $d\oplus(\text{constant }[0])$ with each map extended by the identity on the terminal singleton, which is exactly $j(D)$; and $j$ is injective because $d$ is recovered by deleting the terminal singleton. So $j:D\cong X_0\subseteq W$, and the stages $X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots$ with the same $R_n$, $n\geq1$, satisfy the criterion with $A=j(D)$, giving a relative projective cell filtration of $j$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.8, Observation 6.2.4 and Proposition 5.3.3; relative filtration of the regular module inclusion

proof.text: Both filtrations are indexed by $\omega$ and are continuous at the only limit $\omega$ because $W=\bigcup_nX_n$; the absolute one has its $n=0$ cell $[0]$, the relative one only cells with $n\geq1$, which the statement permits. Therefore both maps are small transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of $D\times\partial\Delta^n\to D\times\Delta^n$. Weights on the one-object simplicial category with endomorphism monoid $D$ are exactly left simplicial $D$-modules (composition is ordinal sum, acting on the left), so $W$ is a cellular weight for that category.

(3) E3: step 4's relative disjointness argument went the wrong direction; replaced by j(D)=X_0 and the filtration X_n for n≥1, with closure of X_n under faces and degeneracies written out. Steps 2 and 5 updated to match. Statement, uses and proof_deps unchanged; no new citations, no tool_uses, no SGA. No duplicate found in the DAG (rg) or in the blueprint; same_as [] is correct.
